ai-hpc.h3: Amazon stock jumps as AWS growth finally outruns AI spending
ai-hpc.summary: Amazon shares rose more than 10% after AWS revenue climbed 37% to $42.2 billion, easing worries that its enormous AI buildout was outpacing returns.
body: Amazon reported that AWS grew 37% year over year to $42.2 billion, its fastest pace since 2021, with an operating margin near 39% and a contracted backlog of roughly $496 billion. CEO Andy Jassy called the cloud unit booming and pointed to a $25 billion annual run rate for AI and custom silicon. Investors rewarded the print because cloud revenue is now growing faster than capital spending.

The company still lifted its 2026 capital expenditure guidance by about 10% to $220 billion, blaming rising memory costs, and warned that capacity will stay tight into 2027 and 2028. The reaction stood in contrast to Alphabet, whose own capex hike days earlier had spooked the market. The message from earnings week was clear that spending is tolerated only when it maps to a metered and growing revenue line.

ai-hpc.h3: Microsoft earnings clear the AI payoff bar as Azure surges
ai-hpc.summary: Microsoft posted strong fiscal fourth-quarter results on July 29 and guided calendar-2026 capex to about $175 billion, with Azure growth reassuring investors.
body: Microsoft reported fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on July 29 with revenue around $87 billion and Azure growth of roughly 43% year over year. The company guided calendar-2026 capital spending to about $175 billion and said fiscal 2027 outlays will keep rising. Shares climbed close to 9% by the next session as investors judged that AI spend is translating into external cloud demand.

The report landed in a tense earnings week where Alphabet had been punished for a capex hike and Amazon still had to prove its case. Microsoft benefited from being able to tie AI infrastructure to a growing and metered Azure revenue line. The result helped steady a stock that had drifted near a one-year low heading into the print.

ai-hpc.h3: Meta discloses $279 billion in future data center leases
ai-hpc.summary: Meta said it has committed hundreds of billions in long- and short-term agreements for AI data centers and compute, underscoring the scale of its superintelligence push.
body: In its July 30 results Meta reported roughly $279 billion in future data center lease obligations and said total AI-related spending commitments now approach $700 billion. The company vowed to ramp AI data center investment significantly through 2026 and beyond as it chases what Mark Zuckerberg calls personal superintelligence. The disclosures put hard numbers on a buildout that spans Louisiana, Indiana, Texas and Canada.

Meta also paired with BlackRock on a roughly $14 billion data center venture in El Paso and confirmed its 5GW Hyperion campus in Louisiana will top $50 billion. Separately the company launched Meta Compute to sell excess AI capacity to outside customers. The moves signal Meta wants to both consume and resell frontier-scale infrastructure.

ai-hpc.h3: Alphabet stock slides after $205 billion capex forecast
ai-hpc.summary: Google parent Alphabet reported strong cloud growth on July 22 but rattled investors by raising capital spending guidance to as much as $205 billion.
body: Alphabet said revenue rose 24% and cloud revenue jumped 82% in its July 22 report, yet the stock fell about 7% the next day. The selloff followed a capital spending forecast lifted to as much as $205 billion, well above the roughly $188 billion analysts had modeled. The reaction set a wary tone for the rest of the hyperscaler earnings week.

The drop briefly pushed Alphabet below its prior $4 trillion valuation and sharpened scrutiny of every big-tech capex line that followed. Analysts framed the week as a test of whether AI infrastructure spending can be justified by external revenue. Google's cloud momentum was strong but not enough to offset sticker shock over the spending ramp.

ai-hpc.h3: TeraWulf rides $19 billion Anthropic lease and sheds Texas stake
ai-hpc.summary: TeraWulf shares gained on a 20-year $19 billion Anthropic data center lease in Kentucky while the miner moved to sell a majority stake in a Texas AI joint venture.
body: TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease worth about $19 billion with Anthropic at its campus on a former aluminum smelter site in Hawesville, Kentucky. The project is set to come online in the second half of 2027 and ramp to roughly 401 megawatts of compute by early 2028. The deal lifted a cohort of AI infrastructure and neocloud names including IREN, Hut 8 and Riot.

TeraWulf also said it plans to sell its majority interest in a 168-megawatt Texas AI data center joint venture for about $450 million. The company framed the sale as a way to concentrate on wholly owned AI infrastructure. The twin moves show the bitcoin miner leaning hard into long-duration hyperscaler leases.

ai-hpc.h3: CoreWeave locks Galaxy Digital Texas campus, doubles capex plan
ai-hpc.summary: CoreWeave leased an entire Texas data center campus backed by $3.5 billion in Galaxy Digital financing and said 2026 capex could reach $30-35 billion.
body: Galaxy Digital arranged $3.5 billion in bond financing for a large Texas data center campus, with CoreWeave agreeing to lease the full IT load under 15-year contracts. CoreWeave separately said it aims to add 5GW of capacity by 2030 and expects 2026 capital spending to more than double to between $30 billion and $35 billion. Most of that is tied to already signed customer contracts.

The company expects to roughly double active power capacity to more than 1.7GW by year-end and plans to fold in Nvidia Rubin systems in the second half of 2026. Nvidia has also committed billions to back CoreWeave's expansion. The neocloud is racing to convert contracted demand into live megawatts.

ai-hpc.h3: AMD secures Core Scientific capacity in $14 billion power play
ai-hpc.summary: AMD struck a roughly $14 billion arrangement for AI data center capacity from Core Scientific, adding a second hyperscale-scale anchor beyond its CoreWeave ties.
body: Core Scientific, which is being acquired by CoreWeave, added a roughly $14 billion AMD deal on top of an existing 590-megawatt CoreWeave contract that already projected about $10.2 billion in revenue. The company had grown to about 437 megawatts of billable AI colocation capacity by mid-July. The AMD agreement broadens the miner-turned-colocation operator's customer base.

CoreWeave and Core Scientific also broke ground on a 100MW facility at the Port of Muskogee in Oklahoma, with about 70MW of critical IT load due to go live in 2026. Once the acquisition closes CoreWeave gains roughly 1.3GW of gross power plus more than 1GW of expansion headroom. The deals show former bitcoin sites converting fast into AI factories.

ai-hpc.h3: Cipher Mining stacks AWS and Google-backed HPC leases
ai-hpc.summary: Cipher Mining has locked in roughly $11 billion in contracted AI and HPC revenue through hosting deals with Amazon Web Services and Google-backed Fluidstack.
body: Cipher Mining signed a 15-year, $5.5 billion lease to deliver 300 megawatts to AWS by late 2026, with the first phase starting in July. It also inked a 10-year, 168-megawatt AI hosting agreement with Fluidstack, a deal backed by Google and worth about $3 billion over its initial term. Google agreed to backstop $1.4 billion of the lease obligations and received warrants for Cipher shares.

The company's first-quarter 2026 materials pointed to roughly $11.4 billion in contracted revenue as its business tilts from bitcoin toward HPC hosting. Cipher joins a wave of miners repurposing power-rich sites for hyperscalers. The combined backlog establishes it as a credible AI infrastructure developer.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI and Oracle expand Stargate toward 7 gigawatts
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank added five new US Stargate data center sites, pushing planned capacity near 7GW and total investment past $400 billion.
body: OpenAI said it agreed with Oracle to develop up to 4.5GW of additional Stargate capacity as part of a partnership that exceeds $300 billion over five years. The companies, joined by SoftBank, named five new US sites including locations in Shackelford County, Texas and Dona Ana County, New Mexico. Combined with Abilene and CoreWeave projects, planned Stargate capacity nears 7GW.

The expansion lifts total planned Stargate investment above $400 billion over three years. It underscores how OpenAI is racing to lock in power and buildings well ahead of demand. Oracle has become a central financier and developer for the flagship AI infrastructure program.

ai-hpc.h3: Neocloud trade wobbles as Nebius sinks on financing doubts
ai-hpc.summary: Nebius shares tumbled after an asset-light pivot failed to answer a key financing question, exposing fragility in the high-flying AI neocloud sector.
body: Nebius unveiled an asset-light strategy meant to outmaneuver CoreWeave but the stock cratered double digits as investors punished an unresolved financing question. The selloff dragged on peers and reignited debate about how much of the GPU boom rests on circular financing between Nvidia and its cloud customers. Analysts began weighing which neoclouds can actually fund their commitments.

Nebius had earlier reported explosive revenue growth and raised annual capex guidance to as much as $25 billion. The reversal showed how quickly sentiment can flip when balance sheets and power access come into question. The episode reframed the sector's contest from a GPU race toward a war over power and financing.

ai-hpc.h3: Bitcoin miners face a 2026 reckoning between AI pivots and margins
ai-hpc.summary: Post-halving margin pressure is pushing bitcoin miners toward AI and HPC hosting, with power-rich sites becoming the industry's main survival strategy.
body: Industry trackers describe 2026 as a reckoning for bitcoin miners squeezed by thin post-halving margins, rising debt and consolidation. Many are repurposing large-scale power and cooling infrastructure for AI and high-performance computing rather than SHA-256 hashing. The shift has turned once-struggling miners into sought-after hosts for hyperscalers.

Early movers like HIVE began pivoting toward HPC years ago, and names such as TeraWulf, IREN, Core Scientific and Cipher have since signed multibillion-dollar leases. Data from TheMinerMag showed 2025 as one of the harshest margin environments on record. The AI pivot has become the clearest path to survival and even outsized valuations.

ai-hpc.h3: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5 with an effort dial
ai-hpc.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on July 24 with a 1M-token context window and a setting that lets users trade off cost against capability.
body: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on July 24, positioning it for complex agentic coding and enterprise work. The model offers a 1M-token context window, up to 128K output tokens and adaptive thinking by default. A standout feature lets users toggle effort between low, medium and high to balance spending and performance.

Opus 5 is priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, unchanged from the prior Opus release. Anthropic says it delivers performance close to its most powerful model on many tasks at a lower cost. The launch continued a rapid-fire summer of frontier model releases.

ai-hpc.h3: DeepSeek ships official V4-Flash as China price war heats up
ai-hpc.summary: DeepSeek published the official DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on July 31, touting big agentic and coding gains from re-training rather than a new architecture.
body: DeepSeek released the official DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on Hugging Face on July 31 and moved the flagship V4-Flash API into public beta. The model card states the architecture and size are unchanged from the preview, with improvements coming from re-post-training. The company said agent capabilities now far exceed the earlier V4-Pro preview.

On the API side the model natively supports the Responses format and is adapted for Codex-style workflows. The release landed as Chinese labs push aggressively on price and capability. It arrived days after Moonshot and Alibaba unveiled their own frontier systems.

ai-hpc.h3: Nvidia trims Rubin Ultra and delays Kyber rack to 2028
ai-hpc.summary: SemiAnalysis reported Nvidia cancelled its original four-chip Rubin Ultra and pushed its Kyber NVL144 rack to 2028 after design and customer issues.
body: About three months after unveiling Rubin Ultra at GTC 2026, Nvidia scrapped the original four-chip design and shifted to a half-size version with roughly half the performance, according to SemiAnalysis reporting relayed by Tom's Hardware. The analyst firm tied the changes to PCB midplane problems and customer pushback on the Kyber rack. Nvidia reportedly will not ship the Kyber NVL144 rack until 2028.

Despite the roadmap turbulence SemiAnalysis said the HBM4 supply bottleneck for Rubin is mostly resolved and expects second-half data center revenue about 20% above consensus. The base Rubin GPU is pitched at 5x the inference and 3.5x the training performance of Blackwell. CoreWeave still plans to deploy Rubin systems from the second half of 2026.

ai-hpc.h3: AMD launches MI400 Instinct GPUs to challenge Nvidia
ai-hpc.summary: AMD unveiled its Instinct MI400 series at Advancing AI 2026, pairing CDNA 5 silicon and HBM4 memory to target frontier AI and sovereign HPC.
body: AMD launched the Instinct MI400 series on July 23 at its Advancing AI 2026 event, including the MI455X for frontier AI factories and the MI430X for sovereign AI and HPC. The chips use AMD's CDNA 5 architecture and carry 432GB of HBM4 per GPU, a 50% jump over the MI350 generation. AMD also rolled out Helios AI rack systems and new EPYC CPUs.

The portfolio leans on the open ROCm software stack as AMD tries to close the gap with Nvidia, particularly for inference workloads where its accelerators have gained traction. The MI430X is slated for availability in 2027. The launch reinforced AMD's push to become a credible second source for AI compute.

ai-hpc.h3: Nvidia pushes AI into PCs with RTX Spark superchip
ai-hpc.summary: Nvidia is bringing its RTX Spark superchip to Windows laptops and desktops this fall, extending its bid to own every layer of the AI stack.
body: Nvidia detailed the RTX Spark superchip, which pairs a Blackwell RTX GPU with a 20-core Grace CPU over NVLink-C2C to run AI directly on personal computers. The part features 6,144 CUDA cores and fifth-generation Tensor Cores with FP4 precision. New AI PCs built around it are expected to debut in the fall.

CEO Jensen Huang framed the consumer push as an effort to win at every layer of the AI stack, from data center racks down to the desktop. The move extends Nvidia's reach beyond training clusters into on-device inference. It also opens a new front against rivals targeting the AI PC category.

ai-hpc.h3: Moonshot releases Kimi K3, the largest open model yet
ai-hpc.summary: China's Moonshot AI released the 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 and published its full open weights, rivaling top US systems on frontier benchmarks.
body: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 on July 16, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model it says rivals OpenAI and Anthropic on frontier benchmarks. That makes it the first open-source model in the 3-trillion-parameter class, roughly 75% larger than DeepSeek's V4 Pro. The launch briefly pressured rival AI stocks as investors weighed China closing the gap.

The company published the full weights on July 27 through Hugging Face, including 96 weight shards and deployment instructions. The move continued Moonshot's open-source strategy that began with Kimi K2 in 2025. It cemented the startup's comeback in a crowded Chinese model race.

ai-hpc.h3: Alibaba previews Qwen3.8-Max at 2.4 trillion parameters
ai-hpc.summary: Alibaba unveiled a preview of Qwen3.8-Max at the Shanghai AI conference, claiming its multimodal flagship is second only to Anthropic's top Claude model.
body: Alibaba previewed Qwen3.8-Max on July 19 at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference, describing a 2.4-trillion-parameter multimodal system it claims trails only Anthropic's Fable 5. The preview is available through Alibaba's own products, developer token plans and its Qoder platforms while evaluations finish. Shares in Alibaba rose on the announcement.

The company shipped the claim without benchmarks, a model card or independent testing, drawing skepticism from analysts. The reveal came just days after Moonshot's Kimi K3 rattled markets. It underscored how quickly Chinese labs are trading top-of-leaderboard claims.

ai-hpc.h3: Huawei touts Ascend supernodes and plans to double output
ai-hpc.summary: Huawei showcased new Ascend AI chip systems at WAIC 2026 and is preparing to roughly double production of its flagship accelerators this year.
body: Huawei presented new Ascend AI solutions at WAIC 2026 in mid-July, headlined by the Atlas 950 SuperPoD it billed as the industry's largest supernode. The company also pushed open-source foundational software and industry-scale supernode deployments. The showcase framed Huawei as the anchor of China's domestic compute stack.

Huawei is preparing to deliver roughly 600,000 units of its Ascend 910C in 2026, about double last year, and lift total Ascend output toward 1.6 million dies. Progress with foundry partner SMIC on 7nm capacity is helping ease bottlenecks. The ramp matters as US export limits keep constraining Nvidia's China sales.

ai-hpc.h3: Only trivial volumes of Nvidia H200 chips reach China
ai-hpc.summary: A US official said very few Nvidia H200-class AI chips have actually shipped to China under new licenses despite the policy thaw.
body: A Trump administration export official said only a trivial number of Nvidia H200 and equivalent AI chips have shipped to China against approved licenses. The comment tempered expectations after Washington cleared roughly 10 Chinese firms, including Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance, to buy the H200 with a per-customer cap. The policy had swung from an April 2025 ban to licensed exports.

The gap between approvals and actual shipments reflects lingering friction over supply, demand and geopolitics. Analysts have argued the US is effectively ceding much of the China AI chip market regardless. Huawei's Ascend ramp is filling part of that void.

ai-hpc.h3: Enterprise AI agents outpace the governance built to control them
ai-hpc.summary: Analysts warn that agentic AI is entering production faster than the content, identity and permissions systems needed to run it safely.
body: Industry coverage in late July described enterprises rushing agentic AI into production while governance, identity and permissions frameworks lag behind. Gartner projects 40% of enterprise applications will embed agents by the end of the year, up from under 5% in 2025. That leap is straining the integration and access controls that let agents use company knowledge safely.

Systems integrators are leaning in, with Cognizant standing up a dedicated EMEA AI unit to help customers build and run agentic workflows. The message from analysts is that organizations must first structure their institutional knowledge and access rules. Without that plumbing, autonomous agents risk operating faster than oversight can follow.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI coding and work agents cross 10 million weekly users
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI said its Codex coding agent and ChatGPT Work task agent reached a combined 10 million weekly active users as agentic tools go mainstream.
body: OpenAI reported that its Codex coding agent and ChatGPT Work task agent hit a combined 10 million weekly active users on July 21. The company's GPT-5.6 Sol model reached general availability earlier in the month and runs at high token speeds on Cerebras hardware. The numbers show agentic coding moving from experiment to daily workflow.

Modern coding agents can now execute end-to-end changes spanning hundreds of files while grounded in real repositories and dev tools. OpenAI is also folding browser-based agent features into ChatGPT and Codex as it winds down its standalone Atlas browser. The shift reflects a broader industry pivot toward agents that act rather than just answer.

ai-hpc.h3: China sets first binding rules for autonomous AI agents
ai-hpc.summary: China rolled out what is described as the world's first regulatory framework focused entirely on AI agents, with tiered limits on agent autonomy.
body: China implemented an implementation-opinions framework aimed specifically at AI agents, establishing a tiered decision-authorization system that governs how much autonomy and access agents can hold. Reports describe it as the first binding regime built entirely around agentic AI. The rules pair with earlier companion-AI restrictions that began enforcement in mid-July.

The move arrives as Chinese labs ship agent-capable models like DeepSeek V4-Flash and Kimi K3 at a rapid clip. Regulators appear to be racing to set guardrails before autonomous agents proliferate across consumer and enterprise apps. The framework could become a template that other governments study.

ai-hpc.h3: EU AI Act core obligations take effect on August 2
ai-hpc.summary: A major slice of the EU AI Act's rules apply from August 2, even after an Omnibus package delayed and softened some deadlines.
body: As of August 2 the EU AI Act's core obligations apply to the majority of AI systems on the European market, including general-purpose model governance duties. The rollout follows the AI Omnibus, given final Council approval on June 29, which postponed some compliance dates and amended parts of the law. A new prohibition on AI systems that generate non-consensual intimate imagery was also added.

The Commission has paired the rulebook with a cybersecurity action plan that shifts toward testing AI in secure pan-European environments. US companies operating in Europe face compliance questions tied to the August milestone. The date marks one of the most consequential points in the Act's phased timeline.

ai-hpc.h3: US Senate advances AI bill with state-law preemption
ai-hpc.summary: A federal AI bill cleared the Senate with language that could preempt state-level AI rules, setting up a fight over the balance of regulatory power.
body: The so-called Great American AI Act passed the Senate carrying preemption language that could override state AI compliance requirements if the House concurs. Supporters frame a single federal standard as clarity for industry, while critics warn it could hollow out state protections. The measure now depends on House approval to become law.

The debate lands amid a patchwork of global approaches, with the UK advancing its own AI safety bill and China enforcing agent and companion rules. US firms are watching whether Washington will centralize authority or leave states in charge. The outcome will shape how AI is governed across the largest tech market.

ai-hpc.h3: Meta opens a cloud business to resell spare AI compute
ai-hpc.summary: Meta launched Meta Compute to sell excess AI infrastructure capacity, turning its massive buildout into a potential external revenue line.
body: Meta announced Meta Compute on July 1, a new cloud business that sells the company's surplus AI infrastructure to outside customers. The move mirrors how hyperscalers monetize capacity and could help justify Meta's enormous data center spending. It arrives alongside disclosures of nearly $700 billion in AI-related commitments.

The launch fits a broader theme from earnings week that markets reward AI capex tied to metered external revenue. By reselling compute, Meta gains a demand signal it previously lacked as a pure consumer of its own clusters. It positions the company to compete for enterprise AI workloads against AWS, Azure and neoclouds.
